title: Langflow unauthenticated code execution
subtitle: Langflow · missing authentication on a code-validation endpoint
summary: A Langflow endpoint that checks user-supplied code can be called without signing in, which lets a remote attacker run commands on the server. Upgrade to a fixed release and keep the service off the open internet.

title: Log4Shell, Apache Log4j
subtitle: Apache Log4j 2 · remote code execution through message lookups
summary: Log4j 2 resolved lookup strings inside logged text, so an attacker who could get a crafted string logged could make the server load and run remote code. It affected a huge range of Java software.

title: xz Utils backdoor
subtitle: xz Utils 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 · malicious code in release tarballs
summary: Two releases of the xz compression library shipped with hidden code that tampered with the build and could weaken SSH authentication on some Linux systems. It was found before reaching most stable distributions.

title: MOVEit Transfer SQL injection
subtitle: Progress MOVEit Transfer · SQL injection in the web application
summary: A flaw in the MOVEit Transfer web application let an unauthenticated attacker run database commands, then reach stored files. It was used in a large wave of data-theft attacks in mid 2023.

title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect command injection
subtitle: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS · GlobalProtect gateway
summary: A command-injection flaw in the GlobalProtect feature of PAN-OS let an unauthenticated attacker run code with root rights on affected firewalls. It was exploited before a fix was published.

title: regreSSHion, OpenSSH
subtitle: OpenSSH server · signal handler race condition
summary: A race condition in the OpenSSH server's signal handling could let a remote attacker run code as root on some glibc-based Linux systems. It is hard to exploit and needs many attempts.

title: Exploit Public-Facing Application
subtitle: MITRE ATT&CK · Initial Access
summary: Attackers take advantage of a weakness in an internet-facing system, such as a web server or VPN gateway, to get a first foothold. Patching and reducing what is exposed are the usual defences.

title: Compromise Software Supply Chain
subtitle: MITRE ATT&CK · Initial Access · sub-technique of T1195
summary: Attackers tamper with software before customers receive it, for example by altering source code, build tooling or update packages, so that the harm arrives through a trusted route.

title: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
subtitle: CWE · weakness type
summary: A feature that can change data or run code does not check who is asking. Anyone who can reach it can use it, so critical functions should always require a verified identity.

title: KEV (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities)
subtitle: Term · CISA catalogue
summary: A list kept by the US cyber agency CISA of vulnerabilities that are known to be used in real attacks. Being on it is a strong sign a flaw should be fixed first.

title: EPSS (Exploit Prediction Scoring System)
subtitle: Term · FIRST scoring model
summary: A daily score from 0 to 1 estimating how likely a vulnerability is to be exploited in the next 30 days. It complements severity scores such as CVSS by describing likelihood rather than impact.

summary: Invented sample: Example Co. reports that a customer database reachable from example.com was exposed for several days. This record only shows how a breach entry looks.

subtitle: Example Co. · invented sample record

title: Example Co. assistant leaks prompt data
subtitle: Example Co. · invented sample record
summary: Invented sample: a chat assistant run by Example Co. on example.com revealed parts of its hidden instructions to a user. This record only shows how an AI incident entry looks.

title: example-colour-utils malicious package
subtitle: Example Co. · invented sample record
summary: Invented sample: a package named example-colour-utils, published by Example Co. on example.com, was found to send environment variables to a remote server on install. This record only shows how the entry looks.
